name: Does a walk-in shower require a glass door or can it be doorless?

mainEntity.name: Does a walk-in shower require a glass door or can it be doorless?

acceptedAnswer.text: A walk-in shower can be enclosed with frameless or semi-frameless glass panels, or left completely open as a wet-room style shower. Open walk-in layouts eliminate glass doors altogether, which removes door tracks and cuts down on routine cleaning. However, open designs require a larger footprint, typically at least four to five feet deep, and careful showerhead placement to prevent overspray from reaching dry bathroom zones. Fully enclosed or glass-partitioned walk-ins retain heat better and keep water confined, making them a practical choice for smaller or mid-sized residential bathrooms.
acceptedAnswer.description: A walk-in shower can be doorless if the enclosure has enough depth to control overspray; smaller bathrooms generally benefit from glass panels or doors to contain water.
